# Data sources and methods

## 1. Generated file

This file is generated by `npm run data`. Do not edit it by hand.

Initial data and events come from real open data. Policy outcomes are simulated, not predicted.

## 2. Output format

- The JSON files use 2-space indentation. An array of plain values and an object of plain values each fit on one line.
- Keys appear in a fixed order. Entries appear in a fixed order: districts by ascending district code, indicators and policy series in the order of the tables below, quarters from 2015Q1 to 2025Q4.
- Every number is rounded once, half away from zero, to the number of decimals of its field:
  - districts.json areaKm2: 2 decimals
  - districts.json centroid: 5 decimals
  - districts.json geometry: 5 decimals
  - history.json population: 0 decimals
  - history.json moveIn: 0 decimals
  - history.json moveOut: 0 decimals
  - history.json relativeMedianIncome: 4 decimals
  - history.json householdIncome: 0 decimals
  - history.json salePrice: 0 decimals
  - history.json medianTotalPrice: 0 decimals
  - history.json rent: 1 decimals
  - history.json mrtEntries: 0 decimals
  - history.json socialHousingCompletions: 0 decimals
  - history.json socialHousingStock: 0 decimals
  - history.json lowUseHousingCount: 0 decimals
  - history.json lowUseHousingRate: 2 decimals
  - history.json cityDisposableIncome: 0 decimals
  - history.json priceToIncomeRatio: 2 decimals
  - policy-track.json socialHousingUnitsStarted: 0 decimals
  - policy-track.json subleaseUnitsMatched: 0 decimals
  - policy-track.json rentSubsidyHouseholds: 0 decimals
  - policy-track.json rentSubsidyAmountPerHousehold: 0 decimals
  - policy-track.json holdingTaxRateLowestTier: 2 decimals
  - policy-track.json holdingTaxRateHighestTier: 2 decimals
  - policy-track.json houseTaxRevenue: 0 decimals
  - policy-track.json commuterPassPrice: 0 decimals
  - policy-track.json commuterPassSubsidy: 0 decimals
  - policy-track.json commuterPassesSold: 0 decimals
- All files use LF line endings and end with exactly one LF. They have no byte order mark.
- A crash while the files are being committed can leave a mix of new and old files. The next run deletes stale temporary files first, and because the outputs are deterministic, a re-run converges.

## 5. Methods

### boundary-simplify

- Title: Boundary simplification for display
- Kind: estimation
- Inputs: `boundaries/moi-7441`
- Steps:
  1. Simplify the boundary with a fixed tolerance, keeping shared edges between neighbouring districts identical.
  2. Orient exterior rings clockwise (d3-geo convention) and round coordinates.
- Applies to: `geometry`
- Quarters: n/a
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

### commuter-passes-estimate

- Title: Commuter passes sold per quarter
- Kind: estimation
- Inputs: `policy/taipei-dot-2019`, `population/ris-odrp014`
- Steps:
  1. Take the published lower bound of more than 5.15 million commuter passes sold by the end of October 2019 (Taipei City Department of Transportation, reported by Newtalk on 2019-11-27) and spread it over the 564 days from 2018-04-16 to 2019-10-31 as a daily rate.
  2. Weight each city and quarter by the daily rate, the days of the quarter in that period with a pass price above 0, and the city share of the combined resident population of the two cities in that quarter.
  3. Split 5,150,000 over 2018Q2 to 2019Q4 in proportion to these weights with the largest remainder rule, so that period sums exactly.
  4. Hold the daily rate constant after 2019-10-31: add the rounded weight of the days from 2019-11-01 to every quarter from 2019Q4 on. A quarter with a pass price of 0 has 0 passes.
- Applies to: `commuterPassesSold`
- Quarters: 2015Q1–2025Q4
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

### commuter-subsidy-definition

- Title: Commuter pass subsidy per pass
- Kind: estimation
- Inputs: `policy/trtc-products`
- Steps:
  1. Set the city subsidy per pass, on top of the published pass price, to 0 in every quarter, because no local-government share is published.
- Applies to: `commuterPassSubsidy`
- Quarters: 2015Q1–2025Q4
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

### district-area

- Title: District area from boundary geometry
- Kind: estimation
- Inputs: `boundaries/moi-7441`
- Steps:
  1. Project the full-resolution boundary to an equal-area projection.
  2. Compute the polygon area in square kilometres and round to 2 decimals.
- Applies to: `areaKm2`
- Quarters: n/a
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

### district-centroid

- Title: District centroid from boundary geometry
- Kind: estimation
- Inputs: `boundaries/moi-7441`
- Steps:
  1. Compute the area-weighted centroid of the full-resolution boundary.
  2. Report [longitude, latitude] rounded to 5 decimals.
- Applies to: `centroid`
- Quarters: n/a
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

### holding-tax-statutory-minimum

- Title: New Taipei house tax rate set to the statutory minimum
- Kind: estimation
- Inputs: `policy/house-tax-act`, `policy/ntpc-ordinance`
- Steps:
  1. Where no city ordinance rate is recorded for the last day of the quarter, use the lower limit of the House Tax Act range in force on that day for both the lowest and the highest rate.
- Applies to: `holdingTaxRateLowestTier`, `holdingTaxRateHighestTier`
- Quarters: New Taipei, 2015Q1–2017Q2
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

### house-tax-even-split

- Title: Annual house tax revenue split evenly over quarters
- Kind: estimation
- Inputs: `policy/mof-6742`
- Steps:
  1. Round the annual house tax net collection of the city (NT$ thousand) to an integer.
  2. Split it into four whole-number quarters with the largest remainder rule, so the quarters sum to the annual figure.
- Applies to: `houseTaxRevenue`
- Quarters: 2015Q1–2025Q4
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

### income-district-combination

- Title: District household income from city income and district ratio
- Kind: estimation
- Inputs: `income/fia-103066`, `income/dgbas-9415`
- Steps:
  1. Multiply the city disposable income by the district relative median income of the same quarter.
- Applies to: `householdIncome`
- Quarters: 2015Q1–2025Q4
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

### income-relative-extrapolation

- Title: District income ratio extended from the latest trend
- Kind: estimation
- Inputs: `income/fia-103066`
- Steps:
  1. Fit a linear trend to the district ratio over the latest published years.
  2. Extend the trend to the quarters after the last published year.
- Applies to: `relativeMedianIncome`
- Quarters: 2024Q1–2025Q4
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

### interp-annual-quarterly

- Title: Annual values interpolated to quarters
- Kind: interpolation
- Inputs: `income/fia-103066`, `income/dgbas-9415`
- Steps:
  1. Treat each annual value as the value at the middle of its year.
  2. Interpolate linearly between consecutive mid-year points to obtain each quarter.
- Applies to: `cityDisposableIncome`, `relativeMedianIncome`
- Quarters: 2015Q1–2023Q4 (and all of cityDisposableIncome)
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

### median-total-price-pooled-window

- Title: Median total price from a pooled window for thin cells
- Kind: estimation
- Inputs: `lvr/moi-25119`
- Steps:
  1. Count the residential building sales of the district and quarter that pass the sale price filter and have a total price (總價元) greater than 0. The house-price-to-income ratio uses the same sales for its numerator.
  2. When fewer than 10 such sales exist, widen the window to neighbouring quarters by the same rule as the sale price pooled window, counting only these sales.
  3. Take the median total price of the pooled sales.
  4. Dividing this value by the district household income indicator gives a district price-to-income figure; the pipeline publishes the numerator only.
- Applies to: `medianTotalPrice`
- Quarters: thin cells only
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

### migration-2015-seasonal-split

- Title: 2015 migration split into quarters
- Kind: estimation
- Inputs: `population/taipei-dbas-a05002802`, `population/ntpc-124872`
- Steps:
  1. Take the annual 2015 move-in and move-out totals of the district.
  2. Split them over the four quarters using the seasonal shares of later years.
- Applies to: `moveIn`, `moveOut`
- Quarters: 2015Q1–2015Q4
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

### mrt-seasonal-split

- Title: Metro entries split into quarters
- Kind: estimation
- Inputs: `mrt/trtc-133184`, `mrt/trtc-128683`, `stations/tdx-metro-station`, `boundaries/moi-7441`
- Steps:
  1. Assign each station to the district containing it.
  2. Where only coarser totals exist, split them over the quarters using the seasonal shares of available periods.
- Applies to: `mrtEntries`
- Quarters: every quarter of a district with an Active_Station
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

### price-to-income-computed

- Title: Price-to-income ratio computed from city series
- Kind: estimation
- Inputs: `lvr/moi-25119`, `income/dgbas-9415`
- Steps:
  1. Divide the city median home price by the city disposable income of the same quarter.
- Applies to: `priceToIncomeRatio`
- Quarters: 2015Q1–2025Q4
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

### rent-amount-annual-average

- Title: Rent subsidy amount from the 2023 annual average
- Kind: estimation
- Inputs: `policy/moi-169800`
- Steps:
  1. Divide the 2023 subsidy amount by the 2023 household-months and use it for each quarter of 2023.
- Applies to: `rentSubsidyAmountPerHousehold`
- Quarters: 2023Q1–2023Q4
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

### rent-amount-carry

- Title: Rent subsidy amount carried from the nearest published year
- Kind: estimation
- Inputs: `policy/moi-169800`
- Steps:
  1. Use the 2023 per-household amount for every quarter outside 2023.
- Applies to: `rentSubsidyAmountPerHousehold`
- Quarters: every quarter outside 2023
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

### rent-reference-sale-ratio

- Title: Rent from the sale price and a reference rent-to-price ratio
- Kind: estimation
- Inputs: `lvr/moi-25119`, `macro/taipei-dbas-131822`, `macro/dgbas-6019`
- Steps:
  1. Multiply the district sale price by the rent-to-price ratio observed in reference districts.
  2. Move the level between quarters with the rent index of the city.
- Applies to: `rent`
- Quarters: reference districts not covered by MOI rent statistics
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

### rent-reference-stats

- Title: Rent from MOI rent statistics for reference districts
- Kind: estimation
- Inputs: `rent/moi-rent-stats`, `macro/taipei-dbas-131822`, `macro/dgbas-6019`
- Steps:
  1. Use the published district rent level as the anchor.
  2. Move the level between quarters with the rent index of the city.
- Applies to: `rent`
- Quarters: reference districts covered by MOI rent statistics
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

### rent-relative-cpi

- Title: Rent per m² carried by the city rent price index
- Kind: estimation
- Inputs: `lvr/moi-25118`, `macro/taipei-dbas-131822`, `macro/dgbas-6019`
- Steps:
  1. Compute the district rent level from rental records where enough exist.
  2. Move the level between quarters with the rent index of the city.
- Applies to: `rent`
- Quarters: 2015Q1–2025Q4, districts with ≥ 30 records
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

### sale-price-pooled-window

- Title: Sale price from a pooled window for thin cells
- Kind: estimation
- Inputs: `lvr/moi-25119`
- Steps:
  1. When a district-quarter has too few records, widen the window to neighbouring quarters.
  2. Take the median unit price of the pooled records.
- Applies to: `salePrice`
- Quarters: thin cells only
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

### sublease-phase-spread

- Title: Sublease matches spread across the quarters of each phase
- Kind: estimation
- Inputs: `policy/moi-b5010`
- Steps:
  1. Take the cumulative matches of each program phase and channel (city-run or central) published by MOI as of 2026-10-31.
  2. Spread each phase total evenly by day from its start date to the start date of the next phase of the same channel, or to the publication date for the last phase.
  3. Count only the days up to 2025-12-31, round the counted share to whole units and split it over the quarters by counted days with the largest remainder rule, so the quarters sum exactly.
  4. Phase 1 has no published start date; 2017-01-01 is assumed.
- Applies to: `subleaseUnitsMatched`
- Quarters: 2015Q1–2025Q4
- Sets `estimated: true`: yes

## 7. MRT notes

### Border stations

A station belongs to the district that contains its station point. For these stations the point and the street address are in different districts.

- Gongguan: station point in Da'an, address in Zhongzheng
- Taipower Building: station point in Da'an, address in Zhongzheng
- Zhongshan: station point in Zhongshan, address in Datong
- Minquan W. Rd.: station point in Zhongshan, address in Datong
- Shuanglian: station point in Zhongshan, address in Datong
- Yuanshan: station point in Zhongshan, address in Datong
- Yongan Market: station point in Yonghe, address in Zhonghe

### Comparable stations

A station that was not open for a full calendar year in 2015 and 2016 borrows the seasonal shares of one comparable station. Only a station with its own shares can be chosen (open in all 24 daily files). The selection rule: (1) prefer an adjacent station on the same line (previous or next station in line order, from the TDX station IDs, with branch stations adjoining their junction station) that has its own shares; if both neighbours qualify, the one with the smaller distance by TDX coordinates, and for equal distances the lower station code; (2) only when no adjacent same-line station has shares, the nearest station by TDX coordinates that has shares. A transfer station's row on another line does not count as adjacent on the same line. The Circular Line opened on 2020-01-31, so its stations have only neighbours without shares and fall under rule (2).

- 大坪林Y (大坪林): seasonal shares of 大坪林, nearest station by distance (0.00 km)
- 十四張 (十四張): seasonal shares of 大坪林, nearest station by distance (1.39 km)
- 秀朗橋 (秀朗橋): seasonal shares of 南勢角, nearest station by distance (1.59 km)
- 景平 (景平): seasonal shares of 南勢角, nearest station by distance (0.76 km)
- 景安Y (景安): seasonal shares of 景安, nearest station by distance (0.00 km)
- 中和 (中和): seasonal shares of 景安, nearest station by distance (1.32 km)
- 橋和 (橋和): seasonal shares of 景安, nearest station by distance (1.88 km)
- 中原 (中原): seasonal shares of 板橋, nearest station by distance (2.26 km)
- 板新 (板新): seasonal shares of 板橋, nearest station by distance (0.97 km)
- 板橋Y (板橋): seasonal shares of 板橋, nearest station by distance (0.25 km)
- 新埔民生 (新埔民生): seasonal shares of 新埔, nearest station by distance (0.32 km)
- 頭前庄Y (頭前庄): seasonal shares of 頭前庄, nearest station by distance (0.00 km)
- 幸福 (幸福): seasonal shares of 頭前庄, nearest station by distance (1.13 km)
- 新北產業園區 (新北產業園區): seasonal shares of 先嗇宮, nearest station by distance (2.06 km)

### Lines not included

Ridership for the Danhai LRT, the Ankeng LRT and the Sanying Line (opened 2026, after the 2015–2025 range) is not included because no station-level source was found.
The MRT ridership indicator of a district with stations on these lines counts only its Active_Stations.

This is a lower bound. - Station pairs used: 14774 of 15357 fare table rows.
- Pairs excluded, by reason:
  - `same-station`: 159 (examples: BL01>BL01, BL02>BL02, BL03>BL03, BL04>BL04, BL05>BL05)
  - `station-not-in-network`: 424 (examples: BL01>R01, BL02>R01, BL03>R01, BL04>R01, BL05>R01)
- Station codes excluded because they are not in the network: `R01`, `V01`, `V02`, `V03`, `V04`, `V05`, `V06`, `V07`, `V08`, `V09`, `V10`, `V11`, `V26`, `V27`, `V28`.

### Population-weighted centroids

- The district centroid is the mean of the village polygon centroids weighted by village population. The village population is the sum of the six household fields of ODRP019 (ordinary, business and single households, male and female).
- Population source: MOI Department of Household Registration, dataset ODRP019, ROC year 114, https://www.ris.gov.tw/rs-opendata/api/v1/datastore/ODRP019/114. Date retrieved: 2026-11-17.
- Boundary source: National Land Surveying and Mapping Center, village boundaries historical map data (TWD97 longitude and latitude), data.gov.tw dataset 130549, ROC 114 edition, https://www.land.moi.gov.tw/chhtml/DownloadGovDoc?gsno=PY9YAR&gdid=533. Date retrieved: 2026-11-17.
- The two files are joined by the 11-digit village code only. The District_Code is the first 8 digits of the village code.
- 17 unassigned area codes (empty village name, code containing R or P) are skipped with weight 0: `65000020R01`, `65000040R01`, `65000100R01`, `65000120P01`, `65000120P02`, `65000120P03`, `65000140R01`, `65000170P01`, `65000220P01`, `65000220P02`, `65000260P01`, `65000260P02`, `65000270P01`, `65000280P01`, `65000280P02`, `65000280P03`, `65000280P04`.
- Access and egress rule: access(i, s) = min(walk(i, s), road(i, s) + accessTime). The rule takes the smaller of the walking time and the road time plus the access time, because residents far from a station usually reach it by scooter or bus.
- The five districts with the largest distance between the population-weighted centroid and the geometric centroid:

| District | Distance (km) |
| --- | --- |
| Sanxia (65000090) | 6.54 |
| Wulai (65000290) | 6.01 |
| Xindian (65000060) | 3.84 |
| Shilin (63000110) | 3.79 |
| Shuangxi (65000250) | 3.52 |

### Model limitations

- The matrix is one fixed matrix for the 2025Q4 network. It does not change with the rail openings of 2018 to 2023.
- Every off-diagonal cell is estimated with the commute model method. No cell is observed.
- The Taoyuan Airport MRT, buses and the Sanying Line are not modelled.
- Linkou has no station in the model. Its residents reach the network by road at Huilong station (O21, Zhonghe-Xinlu Line), about 7.57 km from the Linkou population centre; for some destinations the road alone is faster. Road speed is a gap value, so Linkou commute times may be over-estimated.

### Survey comparison

- Modelled mean commute time from the New Taipei districts to the Taipei districts: 54.0 minutes.
- Survey figure: about 57 minutes.
- Difference (modelled minus survey): -3.0 minutes.
- No constant, parameter or input was changed because of this difference.

## 11. Parameters, part 1

This section covers the parameter entries of type 1 (values taken from published research) and type 2 (values computed from the open data of this pipeline). For each entry it states the study or page cited, each end of the range with the study that gives it, the inputs and steps, and the data that would replace each assumption. The studies are listed in the order of the entries, and no study is ranked above another.

### Type 1 entries: published research values

#### `socialHousing.rentRatio`

- Value: 0.8 ratio of market rent. Status: secondary.
- Study or page cited: Tenant rent of the social housing sublease and management program: 80 percent of market rent, as reported by CNA (Kaohsiung program, 2021) and Money Weekly (https://www.cna.com.tw/news/aloc/202110270245.aspx).
- Range: 0.5 to 0.9 ratio of market rent.
  - Low end 0.5: Money Weekly: rent of 50 to 70 percent of market rent for disadvantaged households (the low end is the lower bound of that range) (https://www.moneyweekly.com.tw/_Article?AID=59942).
  - High end 0.9: project assumption; no independent source (.kiro/specs/data-pipeline/design.md).
- Inputs and steps (method): The Taipei City and New Taipei City social housing rent rules are still to be checked against the program rules. The high value 0.9 has no independent source.
- Data that would replace each assumption: The assumptions are those stated in the method text. A published measurement of the same quantity for Taipei City and New Taipei City would replace them.

#### `rentSubsidy.passThrough`

- Value: 0.5 share of the subsidy that reaches market rent. Status: secondary.
- Study or page cited: Gibbons and Manning (2006), United Kingdom, about 50 percent, as summarized in Berard (2023), LIS working paper (https://www.lisdatacenter.org/wp-content/uploads/files/2023-LIS2ER-B%C3%A9rard.pdf).
- Range: 0.16 to 0.78 share of the subsidy that reaches market rent.
  - Low end 0.16: United States housing allowances, about 16 percent, as summarized in Berard (2023), LIS working paper (https://www.lisdatacenter.org/wp-content/uploads/files/2023-LIS2ER-B%C3%A9rard.pdf).
  - High end 0.78: Fack (2006), France, about 78 percent, as summarized in Berard (2023), LIS working paper (Laferrere and Le Blanc 2004 report 50 to 80 percent) (https://www.lisdatacenter.org/wp-content/uploads/files/2023-LIS2ER-B%C3%A9rard.pdf).
- Inputs and steps (method): Range ends cited via review; the original tables were not read. The value is the figure for the United Kingdom, taken from a summary and not from the original paper. The studies cover France, the United Kingdom and the United States; no Taiwan estimate was found. Finnish work on the same question is VATT Working Paper 149.
- Data that would replace each assumption: The assumptions are those stated in the method text. A published measurement of the same quantity for Taipei City and New Taipei City would replace them.

#### `commuterPass.elasticity`

- Value: -0.3 percent change in ridership per percent change in fare. Status: secondary.
- Study or page cited: Simpson-Curtin rule (fare elasticity of transit ridership of about -0.3), as reported in Litman, Transit Price Elasticities and Cross-Elasticities (Victoria Transport Policy Institute) (https://www.vtpi.org/tranelas.pdf).
- Range: -0.5 to -0.2 percent change in ridership per percent change in fare.
  - Low end -0.5: Litman, Transit Price Elasticities and Cross-Elasticities: long-run values are larger in absolute size (the individual table entry for -0.5 is still to be read) (https://www.vtpi.org/tranelas.pdf).
  - High end -0.2: Litman, Transit Price Elasticities and Cross-Elasticities (the individual table entry for -0.2 is still to be read) (https://www.vtpi.org/tranelas.pdf).
- Inputs and steps (method): Range ends cited via review; the original tables were not read. The individual Litman table entries for -0.5 and -0.2 are still to be read.
- Data that would replace each assumption: The assumptions are those stated in the method text. A published measurement of the same quantity for Taipei City and New Taipei City would replace them.

#### `ghost.rentThreshold`

- Value: 50 percent of income. Status: verified.
- Study or page cited: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), definition of a severely cost-burdened household (rent above 50 percent of income) (https://www.huduser.gov/portal/node/10587).
- Range: none.
- Inputs and steps (method): none recorded
- Data that would replace each assumption: The assumptions are those stated in the method text. A published measurement of the same quantity for Taipei City and New Taipei City would replace them.

#### `ghost.commuteThreshold`

- Value: 60 minutes one way. Status: gap.
- Study or page cited: Project rule, no study for the value of 60 minutes. The 45-minute low end is a TVBS report on a survey of tolerable one-way commute time (original study unknown) (https://news.tvbs.com.tw/life/832402).
- Range: 45 to 60 minutes one way.
  - Low end 45: TVBS report on a survey of tolerable one-way commute time (about 45 minutes); original study unknown (https://news.tvbs.com.tw/life/832402).
  - High end 60: project rule, no study (.kiro/specs/data-pipeline/design.md).
- Inputs and steps (method): The low end is the survey figure as reported by TVBS. The value and the high end of 60 minutes are a project rule, without a cited study. A MOTC daily transport survey, reported by TVBS in 2017, gives about 57 minutes for trips from New Taipei City to Taipei City.
- Data that would replace each assumption: The assumption is: project rule; no study found for 60 minutes. A cited study or dataset that measures this quantity for Taipei City and New Taipei City would replace it.

#### `rentSubsidy.nationalBudget`

- Value: 30000000000 TWD per year. Status: verified.
- Study or page cited: TechNews (2022-06-30), expanded central rent subsidy program from 2022-07-01 (https://finance.technews.tw/2022/06/30/expanded-rental-subsidy-program/).
- Range: none.
- Inputs and steps (method): The value describes the national program from 2022. No engine rule reads it.
- Data that would replace each assumption: The assumptions are those stated in the method text. A published measurement of the same quantity for Taipei City and New Taipei City would replace them.

#### `rentSubsidy.nationalHouseholds`

- Value: 500000 households. Status: verified.
- Study or page cited: TechNews (2022-06-30), expanded central rent subsidy program from 2022-07-01 (target of 500,000 households, up from about 120,000) (https://finance.technews.tw/2022/06/30/expanded-rental-subsidy-program/).

Filters: 主要用途 contains 住家用 or 住宅; rent and area above 0; keep 出租型態 blank or 整棟(戶)出租; exclude records with a parking space (車位N above 0 in 租賃筆棟數, or 交易標的 containing 車位) and 出租型態 獨立套房, 分租套房, 分租雅房 or 分層出租. Reason: the Ghost rule compares household income with the rent of a reference dwelling, which should be a whole dwelling rented by a household. #### `ghost.shareRent`

- Value: 0.032495705499674184 share of residents. Status: secondary.
- Study or page cited: Ministry of Finance (Fiscal Information Agency), comprehensive income tax statistics by village, income year 2023 (112_165-9.csv); Open Government Data License 1.0 (https://data.gov.tw/dataset/103066).
- Range: none.
- Inputs and steps (method): ghost.shareRent = sum over the 41 districts of population x renterRate(city) x P(burden > 50 percent), divided by the total population; population is 2023Q4. Reference year 2023, the last year with observed FIA data (2024 and 2025 are extrapolated). Household income of each district is assumed log-normal. Its median is the mean of the district householdIncome indicator over the four quarters of 2023, which is the income the engine uses. Its scale is (ln Q3 - ln Q1) / (2 x 0.6745) from the first and third quartile of the district total row of the FIA file for income year 2023, so the spread is that of FIA income: FIA income is per tax unit, not per household, and excludes transfer income (for example pensions, allowances and subsidies), so it can be more or less dispersed than household disposable income. The log-normal form is a two-parameter approximation: it has no heavy upper tail or mass at low incomes, and the tail at a burden near the threshold depends on that form. Renters are assumed to have the same income distribution as all households of the district, although renter households usually have lower income, which would raise the share. The rent of the reference dwelling is the district mean 2023 rent indicator multiplied by housing.dwellingSize. Burden is monthly rent divided by monthly income (annual income / 12), in percent; a household has a rent burden above the threshold when its income is below 1200 x rent / threshold. The renter rate is the 2020 census value of the city (a single-year value) applied to the 2023Q4 population of each district.
- Data that would replace each assumption: The assumptions are those stated in the method text. A published measurement of the same quantity for Taipei City and New Taipei City would replace them.

The log-normal form is a two-parameter approximation: it has no heavy upper tail or mass at low incomes, and the tail at a burden near the threshold depends on that form. #### `ghost.shareCommuteWithin`

- Value: 0.8633022947490726 share of employed residents. Status: secondary.
- Study or page cited: DGBAS, 2020 Population and Housing Census, table 14 (employed residents by place of work), Taipei City and New Taipei City reports; Open Government Data License 1.0 (https://data.gov.tw/dataset/10906).
- Range: 0.7316693928107059 to 0.8633022947490726 share of employed residents.
  - Low end 0.7316693928107059: DGBAS, 2020 Population and Housing Census, table 14 (employed residents by place of work), Taipei City and New Taipei City reports; Open Government Data License 1.0 (https://data.gov.tw/dataset/10906).
  - High end 0.8633022947490726: DGBAS, 2020 Population and Housing Census, table 14 (employed residents by place of work), Taipei City and New Taipei City reports; Open Government Data License 1.0 (https://data.gov.tw/dataset/10906).
- Inputs and steps (method): ghost.shareCommuteWithin = share of the employed residents of the 41 districts (2020 census table 14) whose one-way time in the Commute_Matrix to the workplace district is at most 60 minutes; the range low is the share at most 45 minutes and the range high equals the value. Table 14 gives, for each residence district, the employed residents working in the same district, in another district of the same city, and in another county, city or overseas, and it gives no count by workplace district. Workplace districts are therefore estimated: residents working in the same district have time 0; residents working in another district of the same city are spread over the other districts of that city in proportion to commute.jobShare; residents working in another county, city or overseas are spread over the districts of the other city of the pair in proportion to commute.jobShare. Effect of the spreading, in both directions. (a) Setting commutes within one district to 0 minutes barely changes the share within the threshold, because commutes inside one district are under 45 minutes. (b) Placing the whole category of workers in another county, city or overseas into the other city of the pair raises the share within the threshold when the real destinations lie outside both cities (for example Linkou or Shulin to Taoyuan, and Xizhi to Keelung, are longer trips), so the Ghost counts derived from this share may be under-estimated. Commute times come from the modelled Commute_Matrix, and the census counts are for 2020 only.
- Data that would replace each assumption: The assumptions are those stated in the method text. A published measurement of the same quantity for Taipei City and New Taipei City would replace them.

  - Low end 0: Taipei Metro, commuter pass and TPASS product table (policy/trtc-products): a pass holder pays no per-trip fare (https://www.metro.taipei/cp.aspx?n=CEF54168B23F73B4&s=BB3631329CC1A297).
  - High end 30.602311470654936: TDX Rail/Metro ODFare, Taipei Metro (TRTC), New Taipei Metro (NTMC), Danhai LRT (NTDLRT) and Ankeng LRT (NTALRT), adult single-journey full fare, Ministry of Transport and Communications (https://tdx.transportdata.tw/api/basic/v2/Rail/Metro/ODFare/{TRTC,NTMC,NTDLRT,NTALRT}?%24format=JSON).
- Inputs and steps (method): Regression: least squares with an intercept of the adult full fare (TWD) on the rail-graph in-vehicle path time (minutes) over 14774 station pairs gives 0.6955 TWD per minute per trip; value is this slope multiplied by the monthly trips. Selection: high is the larger of value and the same regression over the Uncapped_Range multiplied by the monthly trips, 0.6928 TWD per minute per trip. The Uncapped_Range is the 14603 pairs with a path time below 59.783333333333324 minutes, the shortest pair charged the Fare_Cap of 65 TWD. low is 0, the marginal cost of a minute for a pass holder. Monthly trips: commute.tripsPerMonth = 44 one-way trips per commuter per month, Parameter_Status gap. Fare cap: fares are capped (maximum 65 TWD), so a linear per-minute cost over-estimates long trips. The Fare_Cap affects only 48 of 14,774 station pairs (0.3 percent). The slope does not rise after excluding them (0.6928 against 0.6955 TWD per minute per trip), so high equals value (30.60). The uncertainty range is provided by low = 0. Stations not in the network: R01, V01, V02, V03, V04, V05, V06, V07, V08, V09, V10, V11, V26, V27, V28 do not appear in the TDX station-to-station travel time files or the Ankeng StationTimeTable run times; 424 station pairs are excluded. Migration weights: the fares are cited, but the migration weights (migration.weight*, migration.threshold, migration.share) are gap, so how strongly the commuter pass subsidy moves migration is an assumption. Backtest: the TPASS backtest validates MRT entries only and does not validate migration.
- Data that would replace each assumption: The assumptions are those stated in the method text. A published measurement of the same quantity for Taipei City and New Taipei City would replace them.

#### District job shares

- Method: District share of the 2021 DGBAS Industry and Service Census count of persons engaged (從業員工人數, table 10, owners and unpaid family workers included), divided by the total of the 41 districts. The census excludes government agencies, schools and the armed forces, so districts where public employers concentrate (for example Zhongzheng) are under-counted.
- Note on the census totals: The DGBAS press release published earlier gives 1,888,029 persons engaged for Taipei City and 1,413,606 for New Taipei City. The tables use the totals printed in the census reports (1,885,704 and 1,415,275, table 10, page 140), because the district rows sum to those figures.

#### Commute cost per minute: method

Regression: least squares with an intercept of the adult full fare (TWD) on the rail-graph in-vehicle path time (minutes) over 14774 station pairs gives 0.6955 TWD per minute per trip; value is this slope multiplied by the monthly trips. Selection: high is the larger of value and the same regression over the Uncapped_Range multiplied by the monthly trips, 0.6928 TWD per minute per trip. The Uncapped_Range is the 14603 pairs with a path time below 59.783333333333324 minutes, the shortest pair charged the Fare_Cap of 65 TWD. low is 0, the marginal cost of a minute for a pass holder. Monthly trips: commute.tripsPerMonth = 44 one-way trips per commuter per month, Parameter_Status gap. Fare cap: fares are capped (maximum 65 TWD), so a linear per-minute cost over-estimates long trips. The Fare_Cap affects only 48 of 14,774 station pairs (0.3 percent). The slope does not rise after excluding them (0.6928 against 0.6955 TWD per minute per trip), so high equals value (30.60). The uncertainty range is provided by low = 0. Stations not in the network: R01, V01, V02, V03, V04, V05, V06, V07, V08, V09, V10, V11, V26, V27, V28 do not appear in the TDX station-to-station travel time files or the Ankeng StationTimeTable run times; 424 station pairs are excluded. Migration weights: the fares are cited, but the migration weights (migration.weight*, migration.threshold, migration.share) are gap, so how strongly the commuter pass subsidy moves migration is an assumption. Backtest: the TPASS backtest validates MRT entries only and does not validate migration.

| `limit.socialHousing.unitsStarted.min` | Absent: the lower limit is the lower factor times the real value (budget.ts, checkLimit). |
| `limit.socialHousing.unitsStarted.max` | Absent: the upper limit is the upper factor times the real value, raised to the upper minimum when that is present (budget.ts, checkLimit). |

| `rentSubsidy.costSchedule` | Absent: the whole cost is charged once at offset 0, with share 1 (budget.ts, costSchedule). |
| `budget.ceiling.<tool>.<year>` | Absent: the ceiling of the tool for that year is the Annual_Budget of the year (budget.ts, plan ceilings). |

## 13. Low-use housing

The indicators `lowUseHousingCount` and `lowUseHousingRate` give, for each district, the number and the share of dwellings with an average monthly electricity use of at most 60 kWh. A district has a value only for the half-years in which the MOI published one.

### Source

- Source id: `housing/moi-low-use`
- Agency: MOI (Real Estate Information Platform)
- Dataset: 低度使用(用電)住宅統計結果查詢(縣市及鄉鎮市區) (Low-use (low electricity use) housing statistics by district)
- URL: https://pip.moi.gov.tw/Publicize/Info/E1040
- Years covered: 2015–2025
- License: not stated

### Period convention

A period is written YYYYH1 or YYYYH2. The published value of a period is the state at the last day of the period, so it applies to the last quarter of the period only: Q2 for the first half and Q4 for the second half. That quarter is the Reference_Quarter, and its value carries the period label in `dataPeriod`.

The annual values of ROC years 104 to 108 are mapped to 2015H2 to 2019H2 of the same calendar year. Their Reference_Quarter is Q4, which matches the last day of the year. No first-half period exists for 2015 to 2019, so Q2 of each year from 2015 to 2019 is `null`.

Every other quarter that no published period covers is `null` with the estimate flag `false`. No value is estimated, interpolated, held, extrapolated or pooled.

### Periods with district values

- Number of periods: 17
- First period: 2015H2
- Last period: 2025H2
- Periods: `2015H2`, `2016H2`, `2017H2`, `2018H2`, `2019H2`, `2020H1`, `2020H2`, `2021H1`, `2021H2`, `2022H1`, `2022H2`, `2023H1`, `2023H2`, `2024H1`, `2024H2`, `2025H1`, `2025H2`

### Current and original methods

The MOI publishes two methods for low-use housing. The current method (現行標準) has annual values for 2015 to 2019 and half-yearly values for 2020H1 to 2025H2. The original method (原標準) has values for 2015H2 to 2020H2.

For Xinyi in 2019H2 the current method gives 4.97 percent (3,741 dwellings) and the original method gives 5.32 percent (4,006 dwellings).

Only the current method is used, because it is the only one that covers 2015 to 2025 with one definition. The original-method files are kept in the raw data directory and are not read.

### Periods without a published value, by district

Every district has a published value in every period.

### Data gaps of the low-use indicators

No district is entirely without a published value.
